# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-27 (Extended v189)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to autumn Year 7. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of the Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Café Corinthe (wine-shop). English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, hill farms of Staveford.

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided to Nerine Prydenridge fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided to Zavus Prydenridge same blood debt claim. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6). In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures was forged. Kassa Brackick whispered that Islan Thornmere had secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7, unverified).

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa later went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead, took lodgings in Salcombe; Fenelle Lindmere followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate, took lodgings in Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek Prydenridge gave up being a miller and took work as a brewer (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband gave solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle Lindmere found work in Elmhaven, moved there (summer Year 7). Marald Corrford followed to Elmhaven within month (summer Year 7). Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew and became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for good and took lodgings in Dungate (autumn Year 7). Vesmira Thornmere went to live in Dungate as well (autumn Year 7).

**Solemn promises**: Elra Corrford gave Matho Stenson solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie Prydenridge swore to Nerine Prydenridge to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work (carry sealed letter to Torton) never begun.

**Property and items**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, and kept it.

## Spring/Summer/Autumn Year 7 Observations

Residents walked long way to avoid muddy square. Road rutted and puddled after thaw. Someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall. Multiple residents hummed childhood tunes: Yera, Rinelle, Zavus, Kadan, Bremira, Rorald Lindmere, Nerine, Lurald Stenworth, Ilrald (autumn Year 7). Volan Stenworth and Kassa Brackick each counted coins twice, came up penny short. Matho, Bremira, Thizek, and Pelia each counted coins twice, came up penny short. Matho Stenson, Thizek Stenenridge, and Volan Stenworth fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Jotho and Havie Prydenridge fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Multiple residents observed river up; others said always was in spring. Ismira asked if it would rain; Fenelle only shrugged. Ismira, Bremira, Ferald argued with carter over oat prices. Havie Prydenridge argued with carter over oat price of sack. Kadan and Rovus talked of weather, harvest, lame horse; discussed salt price scandal. Bremira and Ferald discussed salt price scandal. Havie and Movie Prydenridge talked of weather, harvest, lame horse. "The price of salt is a scandal," said Havie; "A scandal," agreed Ilrald. "The price of salt is a scandal," said Gadrek; "A scandal," agreed Isric. "The price of salt is a scandal," said Kassa Brackick; "A scandal," agreed Volan. Yera, Sebin, Pelia, Bremira, Thizek laughed at stories nobody else found funny. Yera complained of aching back, as usual. Pelia complained of aching back as usual. Luvie complained of aching back as usual (Ostcombe). Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Gulls quarreled over heap of fish heads by steps. Children chased hoop down lane. Cart loaded with turnips creaked past well. Yera bought ribbon at stall and then regretted it. Kassa Brackick bought ribbon at stall and then regretted it. Yewyn appeared tired; Pelia noted this. Tatho, Bremira, Zavus, Fenelle Lindmere, Thizek Stenenridge, Yera Stenworth, Gadrek Prydenridge, Lurald Stenworth, Movie Prydenridge mended torn sleeve by window and said little. Volan Stenworth asked "Will it rain?" and Kassa only shrugged. "You look tired," Ilrald told Isric Thornmere, who did not deny it (Ostcombe). "You look tired," Luvie told Havie, who did not deny it. "You look tired," Vesmira told Movie Prydenridge, who did not deny it (barricade period). Tatho and Istho Stenworth spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Baker's boy late again, line at oven grew long. Bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs. Lurald Stenworth read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Jotho read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Movie Prydenridge read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Zavus and Fenelle read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Frost silvered hedges overnight. Wind came off water with smell of salt and tar. Somewhere dog barked at nothing and went quiet. Rain threatened since morning but held off. Nerine and Volan each watched clouds and predicted rain, wrongly. Havie walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Volan Stenworth walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Isric Thornmere told Vesmira that old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis and Discovery

**Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Upon arriving, Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Valjean understood Cosette was escaping; another was goal of her heart. Soul gave utter roar. Grief surpassed bounds. **Valjean at barricade (24th June evening into 6th June)**: Took aim at fireman acting as sentinel on neighboring roof, smashed his helmet with bullet. When officer replaced sentinel, took aim again, sent officer's casque away. Stared silently at wall opposite during barricade phase. Took no other part in combat than to expose himself. Everywhere present in carnage like providence, picking up wounded, transporting to tap-room, caring for them. Reappeared on barricade in intervals. Nothing resembling blow, attack, or personal defence proceeded from his hands. Held his peace and lent succor. Received only few scratches; bullets would have none of him. Had meditated on coming to barricade/sepulchre but did not attempt suicide.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged she never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of her death as blessing. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie. **Barricade combat (6th June)**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Marius's wound (6th June)**: Shot broke his collar bone; felt fainting and falling. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished. Last thought mingled with memory of Cosette: "I am taken prisoner. I shall be shot." **Cosette's current state (summer Year 7, morning)**: Slept soundly, awoke with sun. First thought smiling; felt reassured. Three days since saw Marius. Certain he would come. Gazed at martin's nest in cornice with profound trouble.

## Barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie (24th-6th June)

**Café Corinthe**: Ground floor with bar; first floor with billiard-table and spiral staircase; cellar via trap-door; lodgings and attics. Proprietor: Widow Hucheloup. **Larger barricade (6th June, dawn)**: Height six or seven feet, stepped construction, paling-stones, casks, wheels, omnibus pole, red flag. Forty-three insurgents. **Three-front fortification**: Walled on Rue de la Chanvrerie (front), Rues du Cygne and de la Petite Truanderie (left), Rue Mondétour (right). Almost impregnable but fatally hemmed in.

**Key events**: Javert arrested, identified as Inspector of Police. Le Cabuc executed by Enjolras for killing. M. Mabeuf, aged eighty, upheld red banner; died heroically; body lay in kitchen on table. Gavroche collected cartridges under heavy fire, struck by bullet, staggered, sank in sitting posture, raised both arms, sang. Éponine's corpse discovered in fold of interior trapezium—livid face, streaming hair, pierced hand. She breathed her last there. Corpses formed terrible pile.

**Final assault (6th June)**: Army attacked with infantry of line, National Guard, Municipal Guard, cannon support. Insurgents fired impetuously; barricade had mane of lightning flashes. Street strewn with corpses. Sustained, inexorable assault; attacking column drew nearer; army closed in like vice. Desperate insurgents knocked at house door seeking escape; no one opened; dead man's head gazed from third-floor window. Enjolras and seven others protected them. In inner court with back against Corinthe, sword in one hand, rifle in other, held open wine-shop door, barred assailants. Shielded men with body, facing entire battalion alone. Executed "covered rose" maneuver with rifle, levelled bayonets around and before him, was last to enter. Door slammed with such violence five soldier fingers clinging to it were cut off and glued to post. Enjolras fixed bar across door, bolted it, double-locked with key and chain.

**Siege of wine-shop and attic combat**: Assailants battered furiously; siege of wine-shop began. By dint of mounting on each other's backs, aiding with skeleton of staircase, climbing walls, clinging to ceiling, slashing at brink of trap-door, score of assailants in utter confusion, majority disfigured by wounds in face, blinded by blood, furious, rendered savage, made irruption into first-floor apartment. Found only Enjolras still on feet. Without cartridges, without sword, held nothing but barrel of gun whose stock he had broken over heads of those entering. Had placed billiard table between assailants and himself; retreated into corner of room with haughty eye, head borne high, stump of weapon in hand. Still so alarming as to create empty space around him. His beauty augmented by pride was resplendent; fresh and rosy after fearful twenty-four hours; appeared indifferent as invulnerable being; constrained sinister rabble to kill him respectfully. National Guardsman taking aim lowered gun, saying: "It seems to me that I am about to shoot a flower." Audacity of fine death affected men; as soon as Enjolras folded arms and accepted end, din of strife ceased, chaos stilled into sepulchral solemnity. His tranquil glance constrained rabble to kill him respectfully.

**Grantaire's death**: Drunken man lying prostrate on small table, breast bent over, head lying flat on arms, surrounded by glasses, beer-jugs, bottles. In overwhelming slumber of torpid bear and satiated leech. Nothing affected him—fusillade, cannon-balls, grape-shot, tremendous uproar of assault. Merely replied by snore. Fall of everything augmented prostration; crumbling of all things was lullaby. Halt which tumult underwent in presence of Enjolras shocked this heavy slumber. Grantaire rose to feet with start, stretched arms, rubbed eyes, stared, yawned, understood. Fit of drunkenness reaching end resembled curtain torn away. One beheld all at single glance. Drunkard opened eyes and was perfectly informed. Ideas recurred with abrupt lucidity; obliteration of intoxication dissipated; clear and sharply outlined importunity of realities emerged.

**Final collapse**: Soldiers dislodged last remaining insurgents who had taken refuge at top of house. Fired into attic through wooden lattice. Fought under very roof. Flung bodies, some still alive, out through windows. Two light-infantrymen slain by two shots from attic while trying to lift shattered omnibus. Man in blouse flung down with bayonet wound in abdomen, breathed last on ground. Soldier and insurgent slipped together on sloping slates of roof, clasped in ferocious embrace, fell. Conflict in cellar: shouts, shots, fierce trampling. Then silence. Barricade captured.

**False rumor (6th June)**: False report circulated that insurgents were mutilating prisoners and headless soldier's body was in wine-shop. This sort of fatal rumor usual in civil wars.
